claims.text: The initial material is as-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxidation or oxygen resistance.
Pack aluminizing will diffuse aluminum into the near-surface region of HfNbTaTiZr.
The treatment will create a thin, continuous aluminum-enriched near-surface layer.
The aluminum-enriched layer will form a continuous and adherent Al2O3 scale under high-temperature oxidizing conditions.
Diffused aluminum reacts with oxygen during high-temperature exposure to form alumina.
The resulting alumina scale will be slow-growing and adherent.
Al2O3 has high thermodynamic stability under the proposed exposure conditions.
The alumina scale will impede further oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr.
Pack aluminizing and subsequent oxidation will not materially alter the alloy's bulk microstructure.
At 1000 °C, pack-aluminized specimens will develop a thinner oxide scale than untreated specimens.
At 1000 °C, pack-aluminized specimens will oxidize more slowly than untreated specimens.
The protective scale will remain thin, adherent, and stable during 100 hours at 1000 °C in an oxygen-containing atmosphere.
After treatment and oxidation exposure, room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within 8–16%.
After treatment and oxidation exposure, yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 will remain within 163–530 MPa.

contradictions.description: The falsification rule labels any yield strength outside 163–530 MPa as significant deterioration, although a value above 530 MPa could represent strengthening rather than degradation. The rule should instead specify a minimum acceptable strength or a bounded permissible change relative to matched controls.
